description: Compatibility fixtures for the Core API boundary. Each fixture is one deliberate deviation from a message that would otherwise be accepted, and states the verdict a conforming decoder must reach. The kind of each fixture says which artifact reaches that verdict, so no row claims more than was run. Run them with: python3 taffy-core/contracts/core-api/codegen/generate.py --verify

verdicts.ACCEPT: The message is valid at this version and is accepted.
verdicts.REJECT_CLOSED_ENUM: A closed enumeration carries a value outside the members this version defines. The message is unsupported and fails closed; the value is never coerced to a known member.
verdicts.REJECT_MALFORMED: The message breaks a shape rule: a missing or extra field, a body that does not match its tag, a presence combination the contract forbids, a truncated or over-long frame, or bytes that are not what they claim to be.
verdicts.REJECT_OVERSIZED: The message is otherwise valid and is refused only because it exceeds a bound the contract declares.
verdicts.REJECT_VERSION: The declared contract version is one this build does not speak, so the required meaning may have changed. The message is refused on the version alone.

kinds.payload: Committed bytes. Decoded by the generated Rust decoder and by the generator's reference reader; both must reach the verdict and the named decoder error.
kinds.enum: A committed document whose closed enumeration carries a value outside the contract. The generated Rust `from_wire` must answer that the value is unsupported.
kinds.bound: A committed document measured against the generated limit constant the product compiles in. The generated Rust constant must answer that the measurement is over.
kinds.version: A committed document at a declared contract version, answered against the version this build speaks.
kinds.record: A committed document answered by this contract's own shape rules - tagged-union exactness, conditional presence, enum pairing, field completeness - in the generator. No shipped decoder runs; the records cross this seam as Mojo, and no Mojo decoder can be driven from a stdlib-only Python generator.
kinds.declaration: A committed schema fragment the schema validator must refuse. This is how a rule about what the contract may declare is executed rather than asserted.
kinds.unexecuted: A rule this contract does not express and nothing here can run. It carries a written reason and is never counted as covered.

fixtures.rule: A payload written by this build is read by this build. The corpus starts from something that works, so every other fixture differs from it by exactly one deliberate thing.
fixtures.deviation: None. This is a ready service with no task, no account and no workspace.
fixtures.note: Without this row the corpus could pass by refusing everything, which is the other way a fail-closed decoder can be wrong.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed. A member outside the set this version defines is unsupported and fails closed; it is never coerced to a known member.
fixtures.deviation: The service availability carries a value no member of CoreAvailability holds.
fixtures.note: The tempting failure is to round an unreadable availability down to STARTING and show a spinner. That would tell a person the assistant is coming up when the payload says something this build cannot interpret at all.

fixtures.rule: Every collection is bounded, and the bound is checked from the length prefix before a single element is read.
fixtures.deviation: The active-task count claims one more task than MAX_ACTIVE_TASKS allows; the elements are not present.
fixtures.note: Checking after allocation would let a four-byte length prefix reserve as much memory as it liked. The refusal has to come from the prefix, which is why this fixture is shorter than the count it declares.

fixtures.rule: The payload declares the layout it was written with. A version this build does not speak is refused before the body is read.
fixtures.deviation: The version word is one past the version this build writes; every byte after it is a valid payload.
fixtures.note: The body being valid is the point. A decoder must refuse on the version alone, before a familiar-looking body persuades it that the layout it is about to read positionally is the layout it knows.

fixtures.rule: A payload is exactly as long as its content. Bytes after the record are not ignored.
fixtures.deviation: One zero byte after an otherwise valid payload.
fixtures.note: Ignoring the tail is how a decoder accepts a frame that two writers appended to, and then acts on the half it happened to read.

fixtures.rule: A payload that ends inside a field is refused whole. There is no partial decode and no best-effort recovery of the fields that did arrive.
fixtures.deviation: The last byte of a valid payload is missing, which is what a disconnect during a write produces.
fixtures.note: The fields that arrived are the tempting part. A projection built from them would be missing exactly the state the writer had not got to yet, and nothing in it would say so.

fixtures.rule: A payload names the codec that wrote it. A frame from another codec is refused before it is parsed.
fixtures.deviation: The eight magic bytes are those of a different Taffy codec; the rest of the payload is valid.
fixtures.note: Two codecs in one process is how a frame routed to the wrong reader gets decoded positionally into a record it was never meant to be.

fixtures.rule: The presence byte before an optional field is exactly zero or one.
fixtures.deviation: The presence byte for the account state is two.
fixtures.note: Treating any non-zero byte as present is the lenient reading, and it turns one corrupted byte into a decoder that walks off into the middle of the next field.

fixtures.rule: Every string is bounded, and the bound is checked from the length prefix before the bytes are taken.
fixtures.deviation: A task goal declares one byte more than MAX_TASK_GOAL_BYTES; the bytes it claims are not there.
fixtures.note: This is the collection rule again at a different scale, and the same reason: a decoder that took the length on trust would allocate from a four-byte field before it had read anything.

fixtures.rule: A string field is UTF-8. Bytes that are not are refused rather than replaced.
fixtures.deviation: The goal's bytes are 0xFF repeated, at the length the payload declares.
fixtures.note: Substituting the replacement character would hand a person a goal that is not what the writer wrote, and would do it silently, in the one field they read to decide whether to trust the run.

fixtures.rule: A bounded number is checked against its bound on the way in, not clamped on the way out.
fixtures.deviation: A task reports one basis point more than MAX_PROGRESS_BASIS_POINTS.
fixtures.note: Clamping to the bound is the tempting fix and it is the wrong one: a progress bar pinned at complete for a task that is not is a lie the user acts on, and the payload that produced it would leave no trace.

fixtures.rule: The contract states which optional fields must be present for which phase. A combination it forbids is refused at decode, not repaired.
fixtures.deviation: The account state says SIGNED_IN and carries no account.
fixtures.note: A signed-in state with no account is the shape that renders an account row with nothing in it. Refusing is what keeps that from reaching a screen, because there is no correct thing to draw.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including one inside a list element. A member outside the set this version defines is unsupported and fails closed; it is never coerced to a known member.
fixtures.deviation: The one probe row's verdict is one past the highest member ProviderProbeVerdictView defines (provider_probes[0].verdict = 11); the rest of the payload is valid.
fixtures.note: The verdict vocabulary grew at 3.40 by exactly the member this fixture steps past, NO_MODEL_LISTED, which a surface reads as 'save anyway'. A decoder that rounded an unreadable verdict to a neighbour would tell a person their key was judged when the payload says this build cannot read what the judgement was; a decoder that dropped the one bad row would show 'never probed' for a provider that was.

fixtures.rule: Every optional string is bounded exactly as a required one is, and the bound is checked from the length prefix before the bytes are taken.
fixtures.deviation: The one roster row's refused_endpoint_host is present and declares one byte more than MAX_SOURCE_HOST_BYTES; the bytes it claims are not there.
fixtures.note: The refused host is text a served document chose (decision 0080), which is exactly why it crosses as disclosure and never as an address. Its bound is the difference between a host a sheet can name and a document-sized string handed to a layout engine.

fixtures.rule: A payload longer than the declared bound is refused on its length alone, before it is parsed.
fixtures.deviation: A measured payload length one byte past MAX_EVENT_PAYLOAD_BYTES.
fixtures.note: This row measures a length rather than carrying a quarter of a megabyte of hexadecimal, which is what a real fixture at this bound would cost. What it executes is the bound the product compiles in; that the decoder refuses at that length is proven by core-api-types' own payload_collection_and_field_limits_fail_closed, which decodes a buffer of exactly this size.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed. A command kind outside the set this version defines is unsupported and fails closed.
fixtures.deviation: The command kind carries a value no member of CoreCommandKind holds, and no body.
fixtures.note: This is the first field a reader looks at, and the one where leniency does the most: a kind rounded to START_TASK would start a task nobody asked for.

fixtures.rule: A different major version changes required meaning. The message is refused on the version alone, without inspecting the body.
fixtures.deviation: A command declared at major version 2, carrying the authorization-redirect body that major version no longer has.
fixtures.note: The fields this build does know are deliberately valid, so the only reason to refuse is the version. Authorization callbacks bypass UI semantics on purpose, and a redirect accepted across a major boundary is exactly the message whose meaning may have moved.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including the ones inside a command body.
fixtures.deviation: A start-authentication command names a provider outside AuthProvider.
fixtures.note: The neighbouring members are all real providers, so a lenient reader would pick one and send a person to sign in somewhere they did not choose.

fixtures.rule: A tagged command carries exactly one body, and it is the body its kind names.
fixtures.deviation: The kind says START_TASK and the body present is the cancellation body.
fixtures.note: Reading the body that is there rather than the body the tag names is how a start becomes a cancel. The tag is the only thing that says what the sender meant.

fixtures.rule: Exactly one body, not at least one.
fixtures.deviation: Both the start and the cancel bodies are present, and the kind names the first.
fixtures.note: Taking the one that matches and ignoring the other looks harmless and is not: the second body is evidence that the sender's own state was inconsistent, and dropping it discards the only sign of that.

fixtures.rule: Every identifier is bounded by MAX_IDENTIFIER_BYTES, and the bound is the one the product compiles in.
fixtures.deviation: A start-task command whose request identifier is one byte past that bound.
fixtures.note: An unbounded identifier is not a formatting problem; it is a field an untrusted caller controls, sized by an untrusted caller.

fixtures.reason: core-api declares conditional presence for PageInspectorSnapshotResult only. Executing this needs a conditional_presence rule binding AuthCredentialResultBody.credential_handle to a SUCCESS status, which is a change to the contract rather than to its corpus.
fixtures.rule: A credential result that reports success carries the handle that success produced.
fixtures.deviation: A successful credential result with no handle.
fixtures.note: The rule is real and it is enforced in the browser broker; what is missing is the contract saying so where the generator can read it. Until then this row states the requirement and executes nothing, which is why it is counted separately.

fixtures.reason: The same missing conditional_presence rule on AuthCredentialResultBody.
fixtures.rule: A credential result that did not succeed carries no handle.
fixtures.deviation: A cancelled credential result carrying a handle.
fixtures.note: A handle on a failed result is worse than the missing-handle case, because a handle is something a caller will try to spend.

fixtures.rule: Records are extended append-only and every declared field is required. A message missing one is invalid at this version.
fixtures.deviation: The credential result omits the flow identifier entirely.
fixtures.note: Defaulting the missing identifier to an empty string would bind the receipt to no flow at all, and the receipt would still look like a receipt.

fixtures.rule: A higher minor version of the same major is additive. A reader accepts the message and ignores the fields it does not define.
fixtures.deviation: A cancellation command declared at the next minor version of this major, carrying one field this build does not define.
fixtures.note: This is the rule that lets the contract grow. Refusing here would make every additive change a breaking one, and would leave two builds of the same major unable to speak. The declared version must be raised to one past the schema in the same change that raises the schema: the version verdict compares only the major, so a fixture left behind keeps passing as a message from a past minor and stops testing the rule it exists for. This one sat at 3.2 from the 3.1 schema until 3.6, four minors on the wrong side of the version it was written to check.

fixtures.rule: The tagged-command rule holds for the workspace commands too; there is no second envelope with looser rules.
fixtures.deviation: The kind says CORRECT_WORKSPACE_FACT and the body present is the export request.
fixtures.note: The workspace commands were added later, which is exactly when a second, more forgiving envelope tends to appear. This fixture is here so that one cannot.

fixtures.reason: Revision freshness is a comparison against state the message does not carry: the revision the service currently holds. No decoder can reach this verdict from the bytes alone, so nothing here can execute it.
fixtures.rule: A workspace command is refused when the revision it expects is not the revision the service holds.
fixtures.deviation: A correction submitted against a revision that has since moved.
fixtures.note: Applying it anyway would silently overwrite whatever changed in between, which is the whole reason the field is on the wire. The check belongs to the reducer, and this row records the requirement without claiming the corpus tests it.

fixtures.rule: A corrected fact value is bounded by MAX_FACT_VALUE_BYTES.
fixtures.deviation: A correction one byte past that bound.
fixtures.note: The correction field is the one place a person types free text that is then stored and re-served, so its bound is the one most worth executing against the constant the product compiles in.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including the export format.
fixtures.deviation: An export request names a format outside WorkspaceExportFormat.
fixtures.note: Falling back to the first known format would hand a person a file in a format they did not ask for and would call it their export.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including the inspector's availability.
fixtures.deviation: The availability carries a value no member of PageInspectorAvailability holds.
fixtures.note: Seven of the eight members are refusals with distinct reasons. A reader that guessed would be choosing which refusal to show a person, and would get it wrong more often than not.

fixtures.rule: The contract binds the snapshot's presence to the availability that promises it.
fixtures.deviation: The availability says AVAILABLE and there is no snapshot.
fixtures.note: An empty snapshot under an AVAILABLE result reads as a page with nothing on it, which is a specific and wrong claim about the page.

fixtures.rule: The same binding in the other direction: a refusal carries no snapshot.
fixtures.deviation: The availability says POLICY_DENIED and a snapshot is attached.
fixtures.note: This is the direction that leaks. Policy refused the read; a snapshot travelling beside the refusal is the evidence policy just declined to release.

fixtures.rule: The inspector's node list is bounded by MAX_PAGE_INSPECTOR_NODES.
fixtures.deviation: A snapshot carrying one node more than that bound.
fixtures.note: The inspector projects a page graph into a screen. Its bounds are what keep a hostile page from deciding how much memory the platform UI allocates.

fixtures.rule: A node name is bounded by MAX_PAGE_INSPECTOR_NAME_BYTES.
fixtures.deviation: A node whose name is one byte past that bound.
fixtures.note: The name is page-controlled text. Its bound is the difference between a projection and a page-sized string handed to a layout engine.

fixtures.rule: A handle crosses this contract in a parameter and never in a reply: an interface is handed over, not returned.
fixtures.deviation: A method whose reply hands the caller back a live connection.
fixtures.note: The direction is the whole of it. A caller that receives a receiver holds the end nobody asked it to hold, and the lifetime the contract described belongs to neither peer any more.

fixtures.rule: Every method carries a written ordinal equal to its position, so reordering the list is not a wire change.
fixtures.deviation: Two methods swapped in the list while keeping the ordinals they were released with.
fixtures.note: Mojo assigns an ordinal by declaration order when none is written down, so this is the shape of the accident the rule exists for: a tidy-up of a source file that silently reinterprets every message a peer built yesterday sends.

fixtures.refusal: a record field cannot carry pending_remote
fixtures.rule: A record is a value. A field of one may not be a handle, however the interface it names is declared.
fixtures.deviation: A record that stores a connection to an interface beside the identity it legitimately carries.
fixtures.note: Records here are stored, copied, replayed and re-encoded. A connection survives none of that, so a record that holds one is a record whose second read is a different object from its first.

fixtures.rule: This contract may not declare a field whose name carries an authority-bearing substring; raw_url and full_url are on that list.
fixtures.deviation: A record that hands the platform UI a document's full location beside the identifier it is allowed to have.
fixtures.note: Full URLs terminate in the trusted browser layer, and the reason is not tidiness: a location is a credential-bearing string often enough that the contract refuses to be the thing that carries one. This fixture is the schema fragment, and the generator's own validator must refuse it.

fixtures.rule: The tagged-command rule holds for the delivery commands too; there is no second envelope with looser rules.
fixtures.deviation: The kind says SET_ASSET_POLICY and the body present asks for an artifact.
fixtures.note: The two bodies differ in what they spend: a policy change costs nothing, and a request may spend someone's data allowance. Reading the body a caller sent rather than the kind it declared is how the cheaper intent becomes the expensive one.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including what the connection costs.
fixtures.deviation: A policy command names a network cost outside AssetNetworkCostView.
fixtures.note: The lenient reading of an unknown cost is UNMETERED, because it is the value that lets work proceed. That is precisely the wrong way to fail: it spends a data allowance nobody offered.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including the request family a person's own endpoint speaks.
fixtures.deviation: A custom provider names a wire family outside ProviderWireApiView.
fixtures.note: The wire family decides how a request body is built and how a response is read, and this enumeration is held equal to the core service's own member for member and wire value for wire value. Rounding an unknown one to a neighbour would send a person's key to their endpoint in a shape neither agreed to speak.

fixtures.rule: A tagged command carries exactly one body, and it is the body its kind names.
fixtures.deviation: The kind says SAVE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL and the body present forgets a credential instead.
fixtures.note: These two are opposites over one provider and both are a single record keyed by provider_id alone, so neither shape refuses the other on its fields. Reading the body that is present rather than the one the tag names would clear the credential a person was in the middle of saving.

fixtures.rule: The composer text a completion is asked about is bounded, and the bound is the one the product compiles in.
fixtures.deviation: A completion request whose prefix is one byte past MAX_COMPOSER_PREFIX_BYTES.
fixtures.note: This is the one field of this command a person fills by typing, so it is the one that grows without anybody deciding it should. Truncating it to fit would send a model half a sentence and call the answer a suggestion.

fixtures.rule: A person's own provider carries at most MAX_CUSTOM_MODEL_ENTRIES models, measured as a count.
fixtures.deviation: A save naming one model more than that.
fixtures.note: The list comes from whatever the endpoint answered, so its length is decided by a server rather than by this product. A gateway listing a thousand models must be refused at the boundary rather than admitted into a status projection that then cannot be published.

fixtures.rule: Every enumeration is closed, including one nested inside an optional record inside a command body.
fixtures.deviation: A saved provider whose detected runtime is a value no member of ServerKindView holds.
fixtures.note: The runtime decides which quirks the request carries. A value rounded to a neighbouring member would send llama.cpp's request shape to vLLM, which answers it and answers it wrong.

fixtures.rule: A tagged command carries exactly one body, and it is the body its kind names.
fixtures.deviation: The kind says REQUEST_COMPOSER_COMPLETION and the body present is the endpoint probe.
fixtures.note: The two commands landed in the same change and sit next to each other in the union, which is exactly where a sender's own switch statement falls through. Reading the body that is there would spend a probe on text a person was still typing.
